subject.title: fix(agent): recover gateway runs before fallback

question: Should accepted gateway runs that remain in flight after recovery waiting return an explicit in-flight outcome, retain embedded fallback, or use different behavior for `--deliver` and interactive stdout runs?
rationale: The related open issue identifies this as a user-visible compatibility trade-off between at-most-once side effects and guaranteeing a local CLI result; implementation correctness cannot choose that default safely.

options.title: Approve reattach-first default
options.body: Keep the explicit in-flight outcome after the recovery deadline and document that at-most-once execution takes precedence over a guaranteed local result.

options.title: Use a delivery-specific hybrid
options.body: Prefer recovery without recook for `--deliver`, while retaining the existing fallback for interactive stdout runs if maintainers prioritize a returned local result there.

options.title: Retain recook-first behavior
options.body: Keep the present fallback as the default and treat recovery-only behavior as a separately designed opt-in or future direction.

recommendation.title: Use a delivery-specific hybrid
recommendation.body: Prefer recovery without recook for `--deliver`, while retaining the existing fallback for interactive stdout runs if maintainers prioritize a returned local result there.

likelyOwner.reason: A current-area owner must choose the public CLI recovery contract; the available context does not establish a named owner.
